question: Should RFC 0018 establish the proposed required/advisory condition model, activation-scoped plugin provider API, and explicit gateway.readiness criteria selection as OpenClaw's v1 readiness contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well-proven, but it intentionally creates durable core, plugin SDK, configuration, and projection contracts that automation cannot accept on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Approve the three proposed boundaries, create the implementation issue, change the RFC to accepted, and merge after the lifecycle metadata is complete.

options.title: Narrow before acceptance
options.body: Keep the canonical core condition model but revise or defer plugin providers or operator-selected criteria before accepting the RFC.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave the fixed readiness evaluator in place and pause or close the RFC until maintainers prioritize this product direction.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the three proposed boundaries, create the implementation issue, change the RFC to accepted, and merge after the lifecycle metadata is complete.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision establishes a cross-cutting core Gateway, plugin SDK, and configuration contract, and repository policy identifies this person as the overall product decision lead.
